texts.preamble: Bhawana Kumari vs Saroj Devi on 22 February, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Sumit Dalal District Judge-04, South-West District Dwarka Courts, New Delhi Mca Dj Adj 43/23 Cnr no. Dlsw01-008895-2023 In the matter of : Smt. Bhawna Kumari W/o Sh. Sushil Kumar R/o 87A, Gali No. 1, Pankaj Garden, Goyala Dairy New Delhi - 110071 ... .... Appellant Versus Smt. Saroj Devi W/o Sh. Mahavir Singh R/o Plot No. 25, Kh. 25/2/9 Pankaj Garden, Goyala Dairy Qutabpur, Delhi - 110071. ..... Respondent Order
texts.facts: This appeal has been filed under Order XLIII Rule 1 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) BHAWNA KUMARI VS SAROJ DEVI challenging an interim injunction order dated 10.08.2023 ("impugned order") passed by the Ld. ASCJ-cum-JSCC-cum-Guardian Judge, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi, in Suit No. CS-SCJ-1083/22. By virtue of the impugned order, the trial court restrained Defendant No. 2 (Appellant herein) from: a. Carrying out commercial or industrial activities in two alleged residential properties. b. Parking large commercial vehicles and loading/unloading hazardous articles in the suit premises. 2. The Appellant contends that: a. One of the properties--Plot No. 77-A, Khasra No. 25/9, Block- H-1, Pole No. 5, Pankaj Garden, Goela Dairy, Najafgarh, New Delhi--is not owned by her but by her Bhawana Kumari vs Saroj Devi on 22 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82130766/ 1 husband (who is not impleaded). b. She holds valid licenses for the other premises she claims to own--Gali No. 1, "87-A," Pankaj Garden, Goela Dairy, New Delhi. c. The impugned order effectively grants final relief at an interim stage. 3. The Plaintiff (Respondent) disputes these assertions, alleging that: BHAWNA KUMARI VS SAROJ DEVI a. The Appellant is misusing residential property for commercial purposes, in violation of municipal zoning laws. b. Any discrepancy in address is a ruse to evade liability, especially since MCD has initiated sealing proceedings under Section 345-A of the DMC Act against the premises identified as 77-A. FACTUAL BACKGROUND 4. The Plaintiff filed a suit for permanent and mandatory injunction, claiming that Defendant No. 2 was running commercial activities in two properties--(i) Gali No. 1, Pankaj Garden, Goela Dairy, New Delhi (hereinafter "Property A"), and (ii) Plot No. 77-A, Khasra No. 25/9, Block-H-1, Pole No. 5, Pankaj Garden, Goela Dairy, Najafgarh, New Delhi (hereinafter "Property B"). Both properties, according to the Plaintiff, lie in a residential zone under Delhi's Master Plan and municipal regulations. 5. The Plaintiff contends that the Defendant No. 2 stores "hazardous, dangerous, and highly inflammable articles" and regularly brings in large commercial vehicles, causing public nuisance and safety hazards for residents. 6. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), arrayed as Defendant No. 1, submitted in its status report that sealing action was initiated under Section 345-A of the Delhi Municipal Corporation BHAWNA KUMARI VS SAROJ DEVI (DMC) Act in respect of "Plot No. 77-A" due to non-conforming commercial activity. 7. The trial court, having considered the Plaintiff's complaints, the MCD's report, and the mismatch in addresses claimed by the Appellant, concluded that the Plaintiff had shown a prima facie case of unauthorized commercial use. APPELLANT'S CONTENTIONS 8. The contentions on behalf of the Appellant are as follows: a. The Appellant states that Property B (77-A) belongs to her husband, who is not a party to the suit, and hence any injunction against her in relation to that property is misdirected. b. The Appellant claims ownership only over "87-A," for which she holds a General Trade/Storage License valid until 31.03.2024. She also references a Food Bhawana Kumari vs Saroj Devi on 22 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82130766/ 2 Safety license (FSSAI) for "Plot No. 162," a different location, insisting she has legal authority to store FMCG goods. c. It is argued that the impugned order essentially shuts down her trade and livelihood, contravening the principle that interim relief should be merely preventive, not determinative. The Plaintiff avers that residential zoning bars commercial or industrial activity, especially storage of hazardous goods. The MCD's sealing action at "77-A" supports the Plaintiff's stance that unauthorized business operations are ongoing.
texts.arguments: b. The Plaintiff alleges that any confusion over addresses (77-A vs. 87-A) is orchestrated to evade legal consequences. Further, no license specifically authorizes the Appellant to operate a commercial enterprise in either "77-A" or "87-A" if they remain zoned residential. c. The Plaintiff emphasizes the nuisance caused by heavy vehicles blocking roads, as well as the risk posed by inflammable materials stored in close proximity to residential dwellings. 12. In the instant case, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has initiated sealing proceedings under Section 345-A of the Delhi Municipal Corporation (DMC) Act against one of the suit BHAWNA KUMARI VS SAROJ DEVI properties (i.e., Plot No. 77-A). Equally relevant is the mismatch in address references (77-A vs. 87-A vs. BHAWNA KUMARI VS SAROJ DEVI other addresses) and the Appellant's own admission of conducting business operations under a general trade license. If the Plaintiff's apprehensions are valid, maintaining status Bhawana Kumari vs Saroj Devi on 22 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82130766/ 5 quo by restraining such use prevents potential irreparable harm to the neighborhood. Hon'ble Supreme Court in Wander Ltd. v. Antox India Pvt. Ltd., 1990 (Supp) SCC 727, held that an appellate court will not readily interfere unless the trial court's discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously.
